newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Church-led panel to monitor Philippine truce.
newsitem.headline: Church-led panel to monitor Philippine truce.

text.p: The Philippine governnment and Moslem rebels ended three days of peace talks on Thursday, agreeing to create a panel of churchmen and lawyers to monitor a proposed cease-fire in the south of the country.
But they said they would need further talks before an accord could be reached on a permanent cessation of hostilities.

The agreement to set up an independent monitoring panel was reached in talks between technical committees of the government and the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) held in nearby Sultan Kudarat town.
The monitoring panel will be composed of Roman Catholic church officials, Protestant lawyers and a representative from the local media, a joint statement said.
It said the two sides would meet again in April to resume talks on a proposed "general agreement for cessation of hostilities" in all areas where MILF rebels are operating.
The MILF, which is fighting for an Islamic state, operates in at least 12 provinces in the southern Mindanao region.
Manila is negotiating a separate peace deal with them after signing a peace accord in September with the mainstream Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF).
The largely Christian country's five million Moslem minority regard Mindanao as their ancestral homeland although they are now outnumbered 3-1 in the area by Christians.
More than 30 people died in clashes between government and MILF forces in nearby Buldon town last month. Both sides agreed on a temporary ceasefire to clear the way for this week's talks.
